title: Apply a discount code at checkout
story: As a shopper, I want to apply a discount code at checkout, so that I pay the reduced price.

acceptance_criteria.text: A valid, unexpired code reduces the order subtotal by the code's percentage or fixed amount and the new total is shown before payment.
An expired or unknown code is rejected with the message 'This code is not valid' and the total is unchanged.
Only one discount code can be applied to an order; applying a second code replaces the first and the shopper is told so.
A code with a minimum order value cannot be applied when the subtotal is below that value, and the message states the minimum.
Removing an applied code restores the original total.

title: Reserve a library book via the API
story: As a library member, I want to reserve a book through the reservations API, so that it is held for me when it becomes available.

acceptance_criteria.text: POST /reservations with a valid member id and book id returns 201 and a reservation with status 'queued' and the member's position in the queue.
A member cannot hold more than 5 active reservations; the 6th request returns 409 with error code RESERVATION_LIMIT.
Reserving a book the member already has on loan returns 422 with error code ALREADY_ON_LOAN.
A request with an unknown book id returns 404.
DELETE /reservations/{id} by the owning member cancels the reservation and moves later members up one position.

title: Cancel a booked ride
story: As a rider, I want to cancel a ride I have booked, so that I am not charged for a trip I no longer need.

acceptance_criteria.text: A ride can be cancelled free of charge within 2 minutes of the driver accepting it.
Cancelling more than 2 minutes after acceptance charges a fixed cancellation fee, and the fee amount is shown before the rider confirms.
A ride cannot be cancelled once the driver has marked the trip as started; the cancel button is disabled and a tooltip explains why.
After cancellation the rider receives an in-app notification and the ride status becomes 'cancelled' in ride history.

title: Reset a forgotten password
story: As a user who forgot my password, I want to reset it via email, so that I can regain access to my account.

acceptance_criteria.text: Submitting a registered email sends a reset link that expires after 30 minutes.
Submitting an unregistered email shows the same confirmation message as a registered one, so the form does not reveal whether an account exists.
The reset link can be used only once; a second visit shows 'This link has already been used'.
The new password must be at least 12 characters and must not equal any of the last 3 passwords.
After a successful reset, all other active sessions for the account are signed out.
At most 3 reset emails can be requested per address per hour; further requests are silently ignored.

title: Upload an attachment to a support ticket
story: As a customer, I want to attach files to my support ticket, so that the support agent can see the problem.

acceptance_criteria.text: Files of type PNG, JPG, PDF and TXT up to 10 MB each are accepted; up to 5 files per ticket.
A file over 10 MB is rejected before upload starts with the message 'File too large (max 10 MB)'.
A file with a disallowed extension is rejected with the message 'File type not supported'.
An upload in progress shows a progress bar and can be cancelled; a cancelled file is not attached.
Uploaded files are listed on the ticket with name and size, and each can be removed before the ticket is submitted.

title: Verify email after registration
story: As a new user, I want to verify my email address after signing up, so that my account is activated.

acceptance_criteria.text: After registration a verification email with a link is sent and the user sees 'Check your inbox' with a 'Resend' button.
Clicking a valid link activates the account and redirects to the dashboard with the message 'Email verified'.
The link expires after 24 hours; an expired link shows an error and offers to send a new one.
The 'Resend' button is disabled for 60 seconds after each use.
An unverified user who tries to log in is shown the verification prompt instead of the dashboard.

title: Update item quantity in the shopping cart
story: As a shopper, I want to change the quantity of an item in my cart, so that I buy the right amount.

acceptance_criteria.text: Changing the quantity updates the line total and the cart total without a page reload.
The quantity cannot be set above the available stock; the field snaps to the maximum and a notice states the limit.
Setting the quantity to 0 removes the item from the cart after an 'Undo' toast that lasts 5 seconds.
Non-numeric or negative input is rejected and the previous quantity is restored.

title: Filter products by price range
story: As a shopper, I want to filter catalog results by a price range, so that I only see products I can afford.

acceptance_criteria.text: Entering a minimum and maximum price shows only products whose price is within the range, inclusive of both bounds.
If the minimum is greater than the maximum, the filter is not applied and an inline error says 'Min must be less than or equal to max'.
Leaving one bound empty applies only the other bound.
The active range is reflected in the URL query string so the filtered view can be shared and reloaded.
Clearing the filter restores the full result list and removes the parameters from the URL.

title: Enable two-factor authentication
story: As a security-conscious user, I want to enable two-factor authentication with an authenticator app, so that my account needs a second factor at login.

acceptance_criteria.text: Starting setup shows a QR code and a text secret; entering a correct 6-digit code from the app completes setup.
Entering an incorrect code three times in a row aborts setup and a new secret is generated on retry.
After enabling, the user is shown 8 single-use recovery codes and must confirm they saved them before leaving the page.
On the next login, a correct app code or an unused recovery code is required after the password; a used recovery code is rejected.
Disabling 2FA requires the current password and a valid app code.

title: Request a return for a delivered order
story: As a customer, I want to request a return for an item I received, so that I can get a refund.

acceptance_criteria.text: A return can be requested for a delivered item within 30 days of the delivery date; after that the 'Return' action is hidden and the reason is explained.
The customer must pick a reason from a list and may add an optional comment of up to 500 characters.
Items marked 'final sale' show no 'Return' action.
Submitting the request creates a return with status 'requested', emails a prepaid shipping label, and shows the return id.
Only one return request can be open per item; a second attempt shows the existing return.
